🚨 *needs human* — `newimport-api` health 503 on BOTH import nodes · added to KB as `ki-2026-06-27-newimport-export-path-missing-503`
Surfaced during the 2026-06-26→07-02 laptop-outage catch-up (triage was dark ~6d7h; no live alert fired for this — see note on why below).

*What:* `Method.Import.Api` `/newimport/health/check` returned HTTP 503 (Unhealthy) on BOTH import nodes — MSL04 at 2026-06-27T08:44:35Z and MSL03 at 2026-06-27T08:48:09Z. Exactly one dependency failed: `ExportFilePath` → "Export path '/mnt/temp_backups/methodimport/' does not exist or is not accessible." Redis, RabbitMQ, Mongo (MethodImport db), and SQL c1–c5 all healthy; process up and listening on 5090. This is a mount/dir-availability failure, not a crash.

*Why it wasn't paged:* health-probe-only. All request-level DD Import monitors were OK across the whole window — 299551459 (5xx), 299551465 (P95), 299551472 (subscriber), 299551499 (cron). A dropped `/mnt/temp_backups` share fails the health endpoint without producing request 5xx, so it's invisible to the normal alert path. Only the automated SWAT runbook `swat-rb-linux-http-service-investigate-v1` (posted in #team-incident-response) caught it.

Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`#team-admin`)

*Verify / reproduce (run on MSL03 and MSL04):*
`curl -s http://<host>/newimport/health/check`   → expect 200 (was 503)
`mount | grep temp_backups`
`ls -ld /mnt/temp_backups/methodimport/`

*Suggested fix:* remount the share (check /etc/fstab + CIFS creds) or `mkdir -p /mnt/temp_backups/methodimport/` with correct ownership/perms; re-probe for 200. Durable: add a synthetic on `/newimport/health/check` so a future ExportFilePath failure pages without relying on the SWAT runbook.

*Status:* mount state not verifiable from triage (SSH bastion down this session). May have self-recovered — needs an ops check. Same `temp_backups` family as `ki-2026-06-19` (MSL04 CIFS/disk).
